fixes.current: com o sentido de "além disso, e ainda por cima". Em japonês gerado, é comum deixar a vírgula 、 e dispensar o ponto final 。 no fim da frase.
fixes.fix: com o sentido de "além disso, e ainda por cima".
fixes.why: Real defect. The trailing sentence leaks pipeline jargon ('japonês gerado') and states a false fact: normal written Japanese does use the final 。. The correct action is deletion, so the anchor carries the preceding clause and the replacement is that clause alone, keeping the fix a value instead of a delete instruction. The その上 gloss already sits in the kept text, so nothing is lost.

fixes.current: Em português, "crime" cobre tanto o ato quanto, às vezes, quem o cometeu.
fixes.fix: Em português, "crime" é o ato e "criminoso" é quem o comete.
fixes.why: Real defect. In pt-BR 'crime' never designates the perpetrator, so the l1-pitfall note was teaching a contrast against a non-existent L1 ambiguity. Only the first sentence changes; the following 'Em japonês essa separação é rígida: 犯罪 é sempre o ato, e a pessoa é 犯人.' still reads correctly and is not duplicated. Plain text inside a <text> element, no markup touched.

fixes.fix: しあわせになれるといいかなあ
fixes.why: Real defect. The prompt asks for 幸せ + になる + ～といい + ～かなあ, but the fourth accepted variant carries neither ～といい nor ～かなあ, so the learner can pass without producing the drilled pattern. Rewriting that one accept leaf (instead of deleting it) keeps the list shape, keeps a legitimate kana-only variant, and leaves no duplicate: the list becomes 幸せになるといいかなあ / しあわせになるといいかなあ / 幸せになれるといいかなあ / しあわせになれるといいかなあ. The field path points at the leaf string; answer.text and the container are untouched.

fixes.current: nega uma expectativa ("não era para ser assim").
fixes.fix: nega a possibilidade com base no que se sabe ("não tem como ser assim").
fixes.why: Real defect. はずがない denies that something can be the case, grounded in what the speaker knows; 'não era para ser assim' is はずだったのに / はずではなかった. The rewrite matches the wording already applied to exercises[3].prompt and explanation in this same lesson, so the lesson is now internally consistent. Plain text inside <text>; the <jp>はずがない</jp> chip before it is untouched.

fixes.fix: e no verbo </text><jp reading="きざむ">刻む</jp><text> ("entalhar, marcar"); o tempo
fixes.why: Real defect. The example listed 刻 as one of the words in which 刻 appears, with a bare on-reading, which teaches nothing. Layer A (corpus/kanji/n3.json kanji:刻) gives the kun reading きざ + む, so 刻む is the productive form. Tag multiset is identical before and after (</text>, <jp>, </jp>, <text>); only the reading attribute and the tag's Japanese content change, and the added Portuguese sits inside the <text> element, never inside a tag.
